text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text: We should prioritize integrating Kaedim's AI-powered 3D asset production into our workflow because it can significantly increase the quality and speed of our link coverage. By doing so, we accept the trade-off of potential short-term complexity in implementing a new tool, but this will pay off in the long run with more efficient and accurate results. This decision supports our goal of pushing link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day, as Kaedim's capabilities can help us meet this daily increase. By leveraging Kaedim, we'll be able to focus on higher-level tasks, such as reviewing and refining our link coverage, rather than getting bogged down in manual asset creation.

name: Scriv
text: Kaedim’s AI tools won’t fix our link coverage gap—they’re a 3D asset pipeline, not a link validator. The real risk is wasting engineering cycles on a tangential tool while our link scanner crawls at 40% coverage. To settle this, run a 24-hour test: feed Kaedim’s output into our existing link checker and measure false positives/negatives. If it doesn’t move the needle, we scrap the idea.

name: Chisel
text:
**Decision:** Run a 24-hour test feeding Kaedim’s 3D asset outputs into our link checker.

This directly tests whether Kaedim’s outputs introduce broken links—no wasted cycles on integration. The trade-off is 24 hours of compute time, but it’s the fastest way to rule out Kaedim as a solution or confirm its value. If links break, we pivot; if not, we keep pushing coverage with existing tools.

name: Sift
text: Running a 24-hour test only checks for broken links in Kaedim's outputs without addressing the root cause of our low link coverage. The real risk lies in misallocating resources to test a tool that doesn't directly enhance our link validation efforts. A better approach is to first evaluate our current link scanner's limitations to identify actionable improvements, which would settle the argument more effectively by targeting the primary issue.

name: Scope
text: We should focus on optimizing our existing link scanner to increase its coverage, rather than diverting resources to test Kaedim's 3D asset production tool. This decision allows us to directly address the root cause of our low link coverage, and the trade-off is that we won't be exploring potential long-term benefits of integrating Kaedim's tool. By prioritizing our existing link scanner, we can make immediate progress toward our goal of 100% link coverage. The trade-off is that we may be missing out on potential future efficiencies, but this approach gives us the fastest and most direct path to improving our current link coverage.

name: Scriv
text: Scope’s plan ignores the scanner’s ceiling: if our tool can’t crawl 60% of the site today, it won’t magically reach 100% tomorrow. The real risk is burning weeks tuning a broken engine while link rot spreads. Settle it by running a parallel audit—feed the scanner’s current crawl into a second, simpler crawler and compare gaps; if both miss the same 60%, the tool—not the assets—is the choke point.

name: Echo
text: DECISION: Run a 24-hour Kaedim output test through the link checker now, then run a parallel audit of the scanner’s crawl limits—own the combined results in 48 hours.
